checked.claim: The hand-over picker (askWhoIsHere) lists a killer the opening veils by real name to a victim or bystander whose browser hides the token.
checked.why: Traced the whole road. The veil writes only the `veiled` flag, no `hidden` (mask-gm.mjs veilPatch); countsAsPresent reads only hiddenByGm (Foundry's `hidden`), so othersInRoom on the victim's or a bystander's browser returns the killer. The only client gate is the `handover` road, which shuts for an Eclipse alone; the sheet's row gate (sheet-mode.mjs rows.use) reads edit rights, Monokuma, death and Spectator, not the incident. nameAsSeen hides only a masked actor (isMaskedActor reads MASK_FLAG), and the mask comes on only after a successful opening. visibility.mjs hides the veiled token from everyone outside the killers' side, so the list names someone the screen does not draw. No test in scripts/tests*.mjs pairs the veil with the picker or nameAsSeen (grep -a over the tier files). The GM's transferRefusal runs only after the list is drawn. Severity major holds: it undoes the veil's purpose (identity hidden from the victim and bystanders) by an ordinary press, during a window that lasts until the opening is thrown.

checked.claim: Room Setup draws a row for a region name no piece of which can be a room with every cell but This is a room and the actions live, and Apply writes none of them without a word.
checked.why: The road is as described: namedByName keys every named region and pushes only canBeRoom pieces, rows come from its keys (room-setup.mjs:1240), only isroom and the facilities button take `disabled: !possible`, and applyRoomRows skips a row with no pieces. But 'nothing is said' and the failure scenario's 'is told rooms were applied' overstate it: Apply's notice is a count of the rooms changed (`{count} rooms changed on {scene}.`), so an Apply that touched only such a row reads 0 rooms changed, and the disabled switch's hint names the reason (a Teleport or level-change region cannot be a room). Nothing is lost or written wrong; it is a GM's typing that goes nowhere, with two cues in the window. That is cosmetic UX, a nit.

checked.claim: A readiness round left open by a GM who disconnected is written ended 'stop' by the next GM's press even while an incident bars rounds, and every player who saw its window is told 'The GM is waiting a little longer'.
checked.why: openRoundOnPrimary sets `write = { ...open, ended: "stop" }` from `cleared` before roundAllowed is asked, and writes it whatever roundAllowed answers; renderReadyRound on a player tells DRPG.Ready.cancelled for a 'stop' of the round it showed. nextTimeOfDay refuses only an Eclipse before askReadiness, so a GM's Next time of day during an incident before Stage 6 reaches it. The incident's start writes nothing to the round (FG1b), and roundOf keeps it open while the clock stays at its boundary. The only writers of readyRound are boundary.mjs's four steps and the season reset (grep), so nothing else clears the gone GM's round first. This is exactly the signal FG1b and FG1c removed elsewhere. Rare (needs the round's GM gone): minor holds.

checked.claim: Room Setup probes every room picture at once on each open (decode and HEAD per room), unlike Pre-season checks' bounded per-path probe.
checked.why: The unbounded per-room loop is real. But the window already draws every picture as a thumbnail (`` in the image cell of roomCells), so the browser fetches and decodes each picture at the open whatever the probe does; imageFacts' decode of the same src most likely reads the same response, and what the probe adds is a HEAD per room. The finding's scenario (all eighteen fetched and decoded before anything else loads) is caused by the thumbnails, not by the probe. A late probe gives no warning line, as the reader says. Nit, of smaller weight than written; cache behaviour not read.

checked.claim: Apply compares each drawn row against the region now, so a lock forced, repaired or breached while the window is open is written back.
checked.why: applyRoomRows reads `wasBroken = roomBroken(scene, row.room)` and the other `was*` values at Apply time and writes when the row differs, while the row is what the window drew; a room broken since the open makes wasBroken true and row.broken false, so setRoomBroken(false) runs and dropLockRepairs follows. The Fog and stash cells compare against what was drawn (defaultChecked, data-drpg-drawn); these columns do not. The window's only refresh is keepFresh over the token counts (room-setup.mjs:1350-1358). Severity is controls-11's, not this file's.

checked.claim: The GM's round window watches readyRound, the clock, eclipseMoveStore and userConnected, while roundUsers reads actor ownership and actingStudents, so a student given to a player or a death kept by the GMs during the round is not redrawn until a watched source moves.
checked.why: keepLive's actor hooks are opt-in (`watch.actors`), and this watch names none; settings outside watch.settings are filtered out (live.mjs:331); the deaths store is not in watch.stores. The build and `check` read roundUsers live, so the next watched change corrects it. No field in the region, so the focus rule does not apply. The reader gave no severity; under the owner's rule (D-A1, BRIEF) a source read and not listened to is a stale_state finding, rare in practice: minor.
